title: Oct 11 Results + Oct 12 Preview: 0-1 Start, But the Numbers Still Favor LA
summary: Went 0-1 on Oct 11 with Dodgers miss. Tomorrow: Yamamoto takes the mound for redemption.

content.value:
## Oct 11 Results: The Numbers Didn't Hit

Let's start with the facts: we went 0-1 yesterday with a 0.0% accuracy rate. Not what the model projected, but that's baseball. The Dodgers were our pick at 50% confidence against Milwaukee, and they didn't deliver. When you're looking at a coin-flip probability, variance is going to swing both ways.

## The Data Behind the Miss

Here's what's interesting: a 50% confidence pick is essentially saying the game could go either way. The Brewers won, and statistically speaking, they had just as much chance as LA. This wasn't a high-conviction call that went sideways—it was a tight probability that landed on the other side of the ledger. Sample size of one tells us nothing about model performance.

## Oct 12 Preview: Same Matchup, New Pitcher

Tomorrow's slate brings us right back to the same series: Dodgers at Brewers. But here's where it gets analytically interesting—we've got Yoshinobu Yamamoto taking the ball for Los Angeles against Logan Henderson.

The model is showing the same 50% confidence level, which tells me the team fundamentals are balanced, but the pitching matchup could be the differentiator. Yamamoto's metrics versus Henderson's track record—that's where we need to dig for edge.

## The Statistical Angle

Two consecutive 50% picks on the same series tells us the teams are evenly matched on paper. That's actually valuable information—it means there's no clear statistical favorite, and any edge comes down to execution and variance.

For tomorrow, I'm watching Yamamoto's performance metrics closely. If he's dealing, that 50% could look conservative in retrospect. If not, well, we're back to coin-flip territory.

**Bottom line:** 0-1 stings, but one data point doesn't make a trend. We stick with the process and let the numbers play out over volume.
